text: Withdrawals are capped by a daily limit of 5000.00 per account, which the plan never mentions.
The daily withdrawal counter never resets, so the 'daily' limit is in fact a lifetime limit per account.
The daily limit counts only the withdrawn amount and excludes the fee.
The withdrawal fee is capped at a maximum of 25.00, which the plan does not specify.
The 1% withdrawal fee is rounded up to the next cent, not to the nearest cent.
The 1% fee is computed on the amount after it has been rounded to cents.
Amount rounding adds a small epsilon (1e-7) before rounding to absorb floating-point error, which can shift values that sit just under a half cent.
Foreign-currency deposits are rounded with halves away from zero, using the same helper as other amounts, rather than with halves to even.
The foreign amount is converted unrounded, without first rounding it to two decimals in its own currency.
A foreign deposit that converts to less than half a cent is rejected as 'amount-too-small'.
The exchange rate must be positive or the deposit is rejected with the same 'invalid-amount' reason as a bad amount.
Foreign deposits take no currency code, and the history records them as plain 'deposit' entries without the original amount, currency or rate.
A positive amount that rounds to zero cents (e.g. 0.001) is accepted and records a 0.00 entry for deposits, transfers and splits.
A withdrawal of a positive amount that rounds to zero cents is accepted and still charged the 0.50 minimum fee.
Infinity passes the positive-number check and is accepted as an amount, while NaN is rejected.
A repeated transaction id returns success without doing anything, even when the retried request has a different account, amount or operation type.
Transaction ids are unique globally across all accounts and operation types, not per account.
Transaction ids are kept in memory forever, with no expiry window.
Empty or blank transaction ids are accepted without validation.
Input validation runs before the duplicate check, so retrying a known id with an invalid amount is rejected instead of being treated as a replay.
Rejected operations do not record their transaction id, so a retry with the same id can succeed later, for example after funds arrive.
Unknown accounts are created automatically by any operation, including withdrawals, transfers and splits from accounts that never existed.
Querying the balance or history of an unknown account returns 0 or an empty list instead of an error.
Account ids are not validated, so an empty string is a valid account.
Overdrafts are not allowed: a withdrawal is rejected unless the balance covers the amount plus the fee.
Transfers and splits are rejected if they would make the sender's balance negative.
The insufficient-funds check runs before the daily-limit check, which determines which rejection reason the customer sees.
Transfers and split payments carry no fee; only withdrawals are charged.
The withdrawal and its fee are debited together as one combined history entry.
A transfer to the same account is allowed and records both a transfer-out and a transfer-in on that account.
In a split payment, leftover cents go one each to the first recipients in list order.
A split with an empty recipient list is rejected as 'no-recipients'.
Split recipients are not deduplicated, and the payer may be a recipient, so one account can receive several shares.
The payer's side of a split is recorded as one 'split-out' entry for the full amount, not one entry per recipient.
The interest rate is read as a percentage (5 means 5%), not as a fraction.
Interest is simple, not compounded, on the current balance for the given days.
Interest is rounded down to the cent.
Interest that rounds to zero, or a zero or negative balance, returns success without recording an entry or the transaction id.
Negative interest rates are rejected, and zero rates and zero days are rejected too.
Fractional days are accepted for interest.
History amounts are stored as unsigned decimal numbers, so debits and credits are distinguished only by entry kind.
Balances and history amounts are exposed as floating-point currency units rather than integer cents.
History entries have no timestamp or resulting balance.
Rejection reasons are free-form string codes chosen by the implementation.
